models_evaluated: five widely accessible LLMs (names not given in text)

links.outcome: Under-signaling of uncertainty and source attribution in LLM gut-liver axis explanations
links.effect: Item-level analysis showed consistently high narrative clarity but systematic under-signaling of source attribution and uncertainty, yielding over-coherent explanations that compressed conditional associations into mechanism-like claims.
links.quote: Item-level analysis revealed consistently high narrative clarity but systematic under-signaling of source attribution and uncertainty, resulting in over-coherent explanations that compressed conditional associations into mechanism-like claims.

unlisted_practices: Concept-conditioned requirement engineering enforcing provenance, calibrated uncertainty, and separation of correlation, mechanism, and actionability in LLM outputs

screen.reason: Evaluates five commercial LLMs on gut-liver axis clinical questions to assess readability and epistemic integrity/uncertainty signaling; does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
